📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-03-eda-consumer-amqp-stopped-publishing`
This is occurrence #53. Self-recovering AMQP publish-hits gap, benign shape (matches 51 prior occurrences).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `DevOps` (`@devops` / `#team-devops`) — inert text per Hard rule #13. (Ownership-by-Project row says "Integrations" but no active team by that name exists in ownership.md; KB entry itself frames this as an Integrations/DevOps joint concern.)
Playbook: 1) Confirm DD monitor 296641466 in No Data state. 2) ALWAYS check sibling P1 monitors first — 296632224 (Event ingest stopped), 296636101 (Kafka events stopped) — if both OK, core EDA pipeline is healthy. 3) Confirm service:eda_consumer status:error returns 0 in DD Logs. 4) If siblings also fire, escalate immediately (real EDA-stack outage). 5) Not actionable on a single occurrence — this entry exists so repeats are recognized quickly.
Open Jira: n/a

Source alerts (1 total, degraded mode — no Slack permalink available):
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/296641466

*Suppression ratio:* 60 suppressed vs 35 posted (63%) — steady vs last week's 88/54 (62%), gate behaving consistently, not trending toward too-quiet.

One thing most worth doing next week: `ki-2026-07-03-eda-consumer-amqp-stopped-publishing` has sat at `escalated-for-review` for 58 days across 53 occurrences — that's a decision nobody's made yet.

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-05-21-gateway-microservices-timeout`
This is occurrence #680 (every-10th-occurrence resurface — last posted 2026-08-16T20:40:12Z, ~22.5h ago, still within the 24h suppression window, but occurrence count crossed a multiple of 10).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`@admin` / `#team-admin`)
Playbook: 1) Confirm chronic baseline by comparing ES Ocelot.Responder.Middleware Warning volume vs same window 24h ago (note: this occurrence found the naive 24h-ago check misleading — see RCA below; used same-weekday-7d-ago instead). 2) Aggregate timeouts by RequestPath — if dominant paths are all under upstream microservices.methodlocal.int, it's pool-level. 3) Check ki-dns-microservices-method-int-pps-quota first — DNS bursts on the Windows fleet present here as Ocelot timeouts. 4) If DNS is clean, identify the slow downstream path via Ocelot config in ms-gateway-api/gateway/API/ocelot.*.json. 5) Fix options: (a) raise per-route Ocelot timeout, (b) scale microservices IIS pool / shorten recycle interval, (c) profile the upstream microservice under prod load.
Open Jira: n/a — none filed

Root-cause analysis:
  • Query: ES aggregate on `"Unusual number of XHR errors for account" OR "monitors/77419271" OR "GetSyncWidgetInfoAsync"`, window 17:59:11–18:33:11Z (34 min)
  • Observed: 687 hits, 100% service:gateway
  • Naive 24h-ago baseline (Sun 08-16, same window): 9 hits — misleading, weekend vs weekday traffic mismatch, not a real anomaly signal
  • Same-weekday baseline (Mon 08-10, same window): 787 hits (≈23.1/min) vs this occurrence's ≈20.2/min — within normal cycle-to-cycle variance, confirms chronic pattern
  • DD method-ui XHR logs, widened 100-record sample, same window: 66 distinct accounts, top account (bodegatile) 5/100 = 5% — diffuse fan-out, canonical shape (frontend symptom of upstream ms-gateway-api Ocelot timeouts, not account-specific)
  • No co-fire this occurrence with ki-24 (runtime-core RTC p95), Redis-errors, rest-api-5xx, or ms-account-api-latency monitors — all last fired 2026-08-14 to 2026-08-16, well outside this window
